title: heuristic-prefill-sampler-and-decode-merge-for-interactive-workloads
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Introduces a heuristic prefill sampler and opportunistic decode merge to reduce tail latency for interactive workloads. Adaptive chunk sizing and a lightweight handshake rate limiter included. No public API changes.
description:
Motivation: Interactive, low-token requests (chat-like workloads) suffer from per-request kernel startup and small-batch inefficiencies when prefill and decode stages are treated as rigidly separated phases. This PR implements a lightweight heuristic sampler that drives chunked prefill sizes and enables opportunistic decode-merge when the sampler predicts decode can overlap without harming KV cache locality. The change reduces mem churn from tiny kernel launches and improves p95/p99 latency under mixed workloads.

What this PR does (summary): 
- Add heuristic prefill sampler that observes request token-length distribution, recent KV hit rates, and inflight queue depth to pick a chunking strategy per-request.
- Introduce an opportunistic decode-merge path in the scheduler that merges adjacent short-decoding slices into a single kernel dispatch when safety heuristics pass (memory headroom, kv locality, and time budget).
- Handshake rate limiter: a microcontroller that prevents the prefill->decode handshake from overwhelming the decode worker pool; it enforces a token-based backoff when decode backlog is high.
- Expose kernel hint metadata so the scheduler can select a slightly different GEMM/kern path for merged-decode vs standalone-decode, improving throughput for fused slices.
- Small changes to KV cache priming: aggressive prefix warming for requests that the sampler marks as likely to decode soon (reduces cold-kv misses).
- Add perf harness and new benchmark scenario for interactive workloads (100ms/req target class).

Design notes: 
- Heuristic goals are conservative: we prefer slightly smaller merge decisions over aggressive fusion that could increase worst-case memory usage. The sampler is rules+lightweight EWMA; no ML model.
- Merge only occurs when (1) combined tokens < merge_token_budget, (2) current KV miss rate < kv_miss_threshold, and (3) memory headroom > safety_margin. All thresholds are tunable via runtime flags.

Checklist: 
- [x] Unit tests for sampler decision logic and edge cases
- [x] Scheduler integration tests for merge/unmerge paths
- [x] Microbenchmarks comparing baseline vs new logic on 3 model sizes (small/medium/large)
- [x] Docs note for ops (flags and safe default values)
- [x] Feature gated behind runtime flag (runtime.opt.enable_heuristic_prefill)

- feat(prefill): add heuristic_sampler module and unit tests (author: Maya Patel)
- feat(scheduler): opportunistic decode merge path and handshake rate limiter
- perf(kernel): kernel hint metadata and small kernel selection path for fused decodes
- infra: add interactive workload perf scenario and CI benchmark job
- docs: newcomer notes and runtime flags documentation

Files changed (high level):
- runtime/prefill/heuristic_sampler.cc (new) and heuristic_sampler.h (new)
- runtime/scheduler/decode_merge_scheduler.cc (new) and decode_merge_scheduler.h (new)
- runtime/scheduler/handshake_rate_limiter.cc (new)

- tests/integration/test_decode_merge.py
- benchmarks/interactive_workload.yaml
- docs/notes/prefill-decode-heuristics.md

Performance summary (internal perf rig, synthetic mixed traffic):
- p50: ~unchanged (-0.5% on average)
- p95: -14% latency improvement for interactive class
- p99: -21% latency improvement for interactive class
- token throughput: +6% for small request mix (due to reduced kernels per request)
- memory: peak +3% in worst-case fused scenarios (within configured safety_margin)

Review conversation (high level):
- Liam: "Great approach. Two asks: add a failsafe to never merge if memory pressure > 70% and add a unit test that simulates KV churn."
- Maya: "Added memory headroom guard and two KV churn unit tests in commit 4c2a9f"
- Priya: "CI benchmark numbers look promising; please document the operational flags and safe defaults."
- Maya: "Docs added under docs/notes/prefill-decode-heuristics.md with recommended defaults for Dedicated and Hosted tiers."
- Ethan: "Nit: prefer 'merge_token_budget' be expressed in estimated activation bytes rather than tokens; consider follow-up."
- Maya: "Agree - opened ENG-1502 to iterate on activation-byte budgeting (out of scope for this PR)."
- Approvals: Liam (approved), Priya (approved), Ethan (approved after nit fixed)

CI history: 
- Initial CI: fail (lint) -> fixed whitespace and header includes in kernel_hint_registry patch -> rerun
- Benchmark CI: initially flaky on medium model test due to noisy machine; re-ran successfully
- Final CI: pass all (unit, integration, perf smoke)

Operational / rollout plan: 
- Feature off by default. To try in staging: set runtime.opt.enable_heuristic_prefill=true and keep runtime.opt.merge_token_budget conservative (default 64 tokens).
- Monitor: p99 latency, kv_miss_rate, decode_queue_depth, and peak memory. Alert if p99 increases >5% or memory grows >10% over baseline.
- Gradual ramp: start with 5% traffic, 25%, 50%, then 100% with health checks on each step.

Backward compatibility / risk: 
- No API surface changes. All runtime changes are behind a flag. Small increase in peak memory when fusion is chosen — controlled by safety_margin.

Notes for on-call: 
- If memory alerts fire after enabling, disable runtime.opt.enable_heuristic_prefill and revert handshake backoff tunables to defaults.

Merge: Squash and merge. Merge commit message includes benchmark summary and GA notes.
